heroHeadline: Day 372: Indian Army Chief Issues 'Geography or History' Ultimatum — ISPR Calls It 'Madness and Warmongering'
heroSubtitle: May 17, 2026: Indian Army Chief General Upendra Dwivedi warned Pakistan on May 16 at Manekshaw Centre that it must 'decide whether they want to be part of geography or history' — the sharpest public threat from an Indian army chief in the post-Sindoor period. Pakistan's ISPR responded on May 17, condemning the remarks as 'madness and warmongering' reflecting a 'jingoistic and myopic mindset,' and warning any attempt to push the region toward conflict would have 'severe consequences.' The exchange coincided with Pakistan's official 'Youm-e-Tashakur' (Day of Gratitude) on May 16, marked with a 31-gun salute in Islamabad to honour the armed forces for Operation Bunyan-un-Marsoos. The ceasefire brokered May 10, 2025 holds at Day 372 with no Line of Control kinetic incidents on May 16–17. The bilateral freeze remains total: mutual airspace closure in force through May 24, Indus Waters Treaty suspended, no ambassadors exchanged, all trade halted.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
